Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations / next steps

Hi Tim / Alex 	6

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on the deployment-mode side and the next steps I promised to follow up on:

Summary of where you landed during the call
- Primary requirement: Full customer-controlled data isolation for models that handle regulated customer PII/PHI.
- Secondary: Non-production workloads could run on Dedicated capacity if we can ensure no cross-customer data leakage and clear logging.
- Key controls you called out: KMS integration with customer-managed keys, VPC peering or on-prem option, strict network egress controls, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Questions for you (so we can recommend the right deployment):
1) Do you require the control plane to be customer-managed (Private) or is host-managed control plane + VPC peering acceptable?
2) Which data classes must remain inside your network (PHI only, PHI+PII, or all inference payloads)?
3) Any hard latency SLOs for live inference that might rule out on-prem for certain use cases?

Attachments: I'm attaching our SOC2 summary and a high-level network requirements doc to help your infra team review.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to the 3 bullets above.
- If you want, we can set a follow-up with our Head of Security (Laura) + Mateo (SE) to walk the security checklist and network diagram.
- I'll prepare an initial mutual-action plan (MAP) and share the draft after your answers.

Available times for the security deep dive: Thu 5/13 1012 PDT or Fri 5/14 911 PDT 	6 what works for you?

Thanks 	6 looking forward to narrowing this down.

Best,

Marissa 	6 thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications:

Direct answers:
1) Control plane: we need the *ability* to manage keys and network controls ourselves. Preferably the control plane should be customer-managed (Private) for anything that touches PHI. For lower-sensitivity models, dedicated pools are OK but we need guarantees around tenant isolation and no shared KV caches between customers.
2) Data classes: PHI and any PII tied to customer accounts must remain inside our VPC boundaries. Non-sensitive logs and anonymized telemetry can be routed to hosted.
3) Latency: critical path inference SLO is 250ms p95 for live customer-facing requests 	6 on-prem or VPC peering is OK as long as the path meets latency, otherwise we may use Dedicated in the same cloud region.

Also: can you confirm whether Dedicated means a Redwood-managed cluster that still has a multi-tenant control plane (i.e., we give Redwood API keys), and whether any model artifacts or KV caches ever leave the dedicated pool to populate a shared cache? That was a concern from our infra lead.

We're definitely open to the security deep dive. Thu 5/13 10am PDT works for me 	6 please include the security checklist and network diagram.

-Tim

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations / next steps

Thanks Tim 	6 great questions. looping in Laura (Head of Security & Compliance) and Mateo (SE) to cover the technical guarantees and the network checklist during the call.

Short answers up front:
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools and tenant-level isolation. The control plane is still Redwood-managed (we issue API keys), and we operate/patch the cluster. Data isolation is maintained at the tenant boundary in the serving runtime; we do not surface customer KV cache entries to other customers. However, logs/metrics and the control plane communication remain managed by Redwood unless you opt for Private.
- Private VPC / On-prem: gives you full network isolation (VPC peering or on-prem install), a separate customer-dedicated control plane option, and the ability to integrate with your KMS/HSM so that keys never leave your environment. This is the recommended path for workloads that must meet strong regulatory controls around PHI.

What we'll cover on the security deep dive (Thu 5/13 1011 PDT):
- Detailed network diagram & firewall rules (attached: network_diagram.png)
- KMS integration options and key custody models
- Audit logs, retention, and export (how we stream logs to your SIEM)
- Model artifact handling and KV cache guarantees (we will show SE notes explaining cache isolation)
- MAP items and timelines for Private deployment (approx timeline: 6910 weeks depending on region & infra)

I've attached our SOC2 summary and the network diagram for your infra team to pre-review. If you have an internal checklist, please share and we'll annotate it.

Proposed meeting invite: Thu 5/13 1011 PDT (I'll send the calendar invite shortly).

Marissa
